message: Merge develop into feat/terminal-envelope-and-credential-retirement

docs(adr-0059,adr-0060,task-038,task-039): promote the records the code already enforced

Both ADRs still read Proposed, with section 5 in the future tense and
section 6 saying "Nothing yet", although their rules were enforced at
seven crossings. Promoted together because they landed together.

Merge feat/terminal-envelope-and-credential-retirement: credentials retire on cause

TASK-038 / ADR-0059: a voided envelope closed its writes but left its
reads open, and a neutral gate kept minting fresh credentials on every
open. TASK-039 / ADR-0060 retires credentials when a contact is corrected
or an access code reset. Two mechanisms on purpose, not one.

docs(session,envelope,adr-0057): fix three claims the TASK-038/039 merge left false

The worst was in the OpenAPI text of ResetRecipientAccessCodeController,
which told senders to void a document when a reset now suffices. The
other two were a docblock and a clause in ADR-0057. None named the
records the merge touched, so a search by record name could not find them.

Merge feat/terminal-envelope-and-credential-retirement: three claims the merge left false

One published OpenAPI text, one docblock pointing at a closed backlog row
and one false clause in ADR-0057 about the scope of ADR-0059.

feat(task-036): a recipient slot may be declared empty, and named once afterwards

A recipient with no contact was already sendable and inert, and nothing
said whether the emptiness was deliberate. This adds the declaration of a
claimable slot, the claim that fills it once, and the guards around both.

Merge origin/develop into feat/claimable-recipient-slot

One conflict, in SigningTokenIssuance.

fix(task-036): register the claim handler and correct nine prose surfaces

The claim command had a use case, a controller and a route but no
Messenger handler, so it failed with NoHandlerForMessageException on
every path. Also fixes stale docs that pointed at the wrong issuer port,
and adds the tests for the bars that were never written, including the
guard that stops a correction from reaching an unclaimed slot.

docs(task-036,adr-0057): correct four claims about the claimable slot

BL-204 framed ADR-0032 and ADR-0057 as two accounts of one event; they
decide different things. ADR-0057 sections 2.5 and 2.7 also disagreed
about where the guard sits, and door 2 needs three real guards, not two.

feat(task-033): add MACHINE_KEY_ASSERTED and the sender's signs_via declaration

A delegated act gets a name to record on both sides of the mirror, and
the sender declares how a recipient's act reaches us. A recipient
declared MACHINE_KEY carries the neutral gate pair; any other
combination is refused when the envelope is authored (ADR-0055 2.1, 2.2).

fix(task-036): a claim no longer erases a contact it was not asked to change

claim() wrote email and phone unconditionally, so a slot that already
had a mailbox lost it. No fixture had built such a slot. The state
question is now asked before the body question, and the prose written
after the earlier sweep is corrected.
Merge feat/claimable-recipient-slot into feat/delegated-signature

feat(task-033): three doors refuse the link of a delegated recipient

A MACHINE_KEY recipient never opens a link, so a signing credential for
them would only let its holder act in their place past a neutral gate.
The mint, the session open and the issuer census now refuse it, and the
step survives the door that closes.

feat(task-033): record what the integrator asserts, in columns of its own

AssertedEvidence is a closed six-field value in which every field is the
integrator's claim and none is observed. It is stored in asserted_*
columns beside the observed twins, and the asserted document hash is now
a list because one session covers several documents (ADR-0055 2.5, 2.14).

feat(task-033): the delegated act goes through the ordinary commit

The open names its own admission and the assertion is checked against
what we hold before it counts. The commit still goes through
SigningSession::commitSignature() unchanged, so consent, the recorded
facts and completion are identical to an ordinary ceremony.

feat(envelope): add a reminder that does not claim the address was wrong

Re-inviting a recipient only had the contact-correction route, which
costs one of the three corrections reserved for real addressing errors
and records that the sender mistyped the address. A resend mints a
fresh link without either.

feat(task-033): add the integrator's signature route for delegated recipients

POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/signature under
MACHINE_KEY. The controller lives in Session/UI/Http because the layer
rules give Envelope's UI no access to Session's use cases. The visible
mark now says the signature was made via a connected system.

feat(envelope): add POST .../recipients/{id}/reminders and the columns that keep its trace

The sender-facing surface had no way to re-invite anybody. The new route
is shaped like corrections (an appended fact, no body, 204) but means the
opposite, and two columns record how many were made and when.

feat(notification): add RECIPIENT_REMINDER and the ordinal that keeps it from going silent

Envelope emits and Notification observes, the same one-way path the
invitation and the correction notice take, so ADR-0037 is untouched. The
ordinal in the occasion identity stops a second reminder from being
deduplicated away.

test(envelope): cover the resend end to end and its use case

The acceptance test sends, reminds, is refused for reminding too soon,
reads the second mail and opens the same session from the new link.
Also fixes a migration whose version collided with another branch and
a contract that denied its own route.

test(acceptance): make the resend session case assert something that can fail

The old assertion compared two ids derived from the same inputs, so it
was equal by construction. Also brings the docs outside src/ up to date
for the new route and cross-links it from corrections.

feat(task-033): add the machine-driven ceremony for relayed one-time codes

We mint the code, the person reads it on their own handset and the
integrator relays it. That is not delegation: the recorded method stays
the real one (OTP_EMAIL), never MACHINE_KEY_ASSERTED. Covered end to end
over HTTP and real SQL (ADR-0055 2.11).

Merge origin/develop into feat/recipient-invitation-reminder

The branch was cut from a stale develop. Five conflicts, all additive:
credentialsRetiredAt from ADR-0060 and the resend properties on
Recipient are both kept, with the new properties last.

docs(adr-0064,ddd): propose the outbound integrator webhook

The Envelope context map promised a Webhook subscriber that does not
exist: 33 events are published internally and delivered to nobody
outside. ADR-0064 decides the surface; nothing is built yet.

docs(adr-0064,bl-226): correct what the audits found and record the client filter

Nine claims were false, four of them a true guarantee attached to a
mechanism that cannot hold it. BL-226 records that a tenant running two
integrations would get each other's envelopes, and that the client id on
EnvelopeCreated is the axis to narrow on.

fix(bl-152): re-opening the link no longer bypasses the retirement anchor

After a contact correction the wrong mailbox could re-open its live
link and, under a neutral access gate, be minted a credential. The
signing token is now revoked. The acceptance cases were also made able
to fail: one drove the reset through a route that stamps the real clock.

fix(adr-0059): a signer keeps the copy they signed after the envelope completes

One isTerminal() predicate answered two questions and erased the
distinction ADR-0059 section 7.4 draws: a completed envelope's reads are
of a document the recipient signed, a voided one's are withdrawn.

docs(adr-0059,adr-0060,openapi): stop claiming mechanisms nobody built

Six records over-claimed what the branch built. The published refusals
also stop enumerating envelope states, because the list is what
travelled into the signer's code, and two read-side guarantees are now
published where a consumer can rely on them.

Merge fix/signing-link-revocation-on-correction: the retirement anchor holds

TASK-039 specified three commits and one was built. The signing token
is now revoked on correction, so the old mailbox cannot re-open its link.

Merge fix/completed-envelope-keeps-recipient-reads: a signer keeps the copy they signed

A completed envelope refused the recipient who had just signed the read
model and the document bytes. Completed and voided are now told apart
at the three read crossings.

Merge docs/task-038-039-record-sweep: the records stop claiming a mechanism nobody built

ADR-0060 is now Accepted with persistence partial, and section 6 carries
two explicit NOT BUILT rows. The spec stops publishing a list of states.

fix(adr-0059): the second mint site refuses a dead envelope, for delivered methods too

submitAuthResponse() was the only one of the three acts that never
received envelopeIsAlive. Also fixes a published description that gave
a claim and its negation on MintSigningTokenController.

Merge fix/revoked-in-the-published-enum: the second mint site refuses a dead envelope

For OTP_EMAIL and OTP_SMS the flag reached nothing, so a dead envelope
still passed the gate. The spec also stops contradicting itself.

test(task-036): cover the guard that decides who may be claimed, and fix three claims

Nothing executed Recipient::guardClaimable(). Two docblocks had been
adopted by the guard inserted above them, and the replay promise in
the published spec was unconditional where the code is conditional.

docs(task-036): correct premises that survived in the records

"The authoring guard" outlived its rename, "a claimable slot has no
contact by construction" was false, and the published spec said locale
could not be edited while the handoff asked the dashboard to send it.

test(task-036): make two fixtures match their prose and re-read the stale records

The "phone-only" fixture had no phone, so the tripwire could not turn
red. The review cycle also left TASK-037 and three ADRs with stale
status text and links that refused to point at each other.

test(adr-0059): cover the Envelope-to-Session reactor chain and the fan-out lock

Gutting OnEnvelopeVoided left the suite green, and SESSION_REVOKED never
reached the event log in any test. The FOR UPDATE on findByEnvelope()
is now proven from a second connection.

Merge test/reactor-crossing-and-revocation-lock: two properties nothing could see

The reactor chain from Envelope to Session had no test, and the row lock
in findByEnvelope() was unprovable from a single connection.

Merge origin/develop into feat/claimable-recipient-slot

Eight conflicts. Two needed judgement and both are published spec: for
MintSigningTokenController and SigningTokenIssuance develop's wording is
kept because it states the property where ours enumerated states.

docs(task-036): cite the run that covers the tip

Both records cited a green run that predated three commits touching
src/, two of them behaviour fixes.

refactor(task-041): rename the resend away from reminder (domain and adapters)

`reminder` is already taken by RemindersSchedule, which nudges before an
envelope expires. What TASK-041 built re-sends one lost invitation, with
a different trigger, population and copy. This part renames the routes,
events, columns, settings and docs.
refactor(task-041): rename the resend away from reminder (integration tests)

refactor(task-041): rename the resend away from reminder (unit tests)

Follows the domain, application and adapter rename and the test updates
before it, so the noun is free for the scheduled expiry nudge.

feat(envelope): the too-recent refusal says when the resend becomes possible

Asked for by the dashboard. "Wait 15 minutes" is wrong by however long
ago the last send was; the refusal now carries the time to retry.

feat(envelope): lower the resend floor to 60s and refuse a resend with no address

A floor that is too short only lets a sender nag, which is bounded and
visible; too long and the window becomes the outage. A resend to a
recipient with no address used to answer 204, spend the ordinal and log
a send that never happened; it is now refused. Also corrects eleven
prose surfaces found by the branch audit.

feat(envelope)!: make recipient delivery its own dimension, ADR-0065 steps 1, 2 and 4

DELIVERY_FAILED was never an outcome of the recipient's leg; it annotated
a leg still PENDING and overwrote that state. BREAKING: outcome no
longer publishes DELIVERY_FAILED. An unreachable recipient is now
outcome PENDING with delivery FAILED.

feat(notification): a delivery that works is recorded as a fact, ADR-0065 step 3

The delivery dimension could be set but not cleared, because the
Envelope command port had no counterpart to markRecipientDeliveryFailed.
Also fixes the findings of the second audit and a completion-notice test
that could not fail when its guard was deleted.

feat(envelope)!: the delivery dimension is per destination, not per recipient

BREAKING: delivery is now a map keyed by contact point and
delivery_observed_at is gone, each destination carrying its own. A
bounced email and an accepted SMS can coexist. ADR-0065 is promoted to
Accepted and the docs and schema mirror are brought in line.

Merge origin/develop into feat/recipient-invitation-reminder

Nine conflicts, all resolved by keeping both sides: the delivery trace
and the invitation revocation anchor answer different questions. Both
sides had appended a trailing property to the same entity.

fix(notification): stamp the delivery observation at transmission, not at request

delivery_observed_at took the command's issuedAt, which is the instant
the occasion was created, not when the message was transmitted.
Merge origin/develop into feat/recipient-invitation-reminder

Merge feat/recipient-invitation-reminder: invitation resend and the delivery dimension

TASK-041 adds POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/resends with
a reissued credential, its own notification purpose and copy, and a
minimum interval. ADR-0065 makes recipient delivery a per-destination
dimension of its own.

docs(openapi): publish what remains behind each terminal state

The signer needs to know what a recipient still has behind COMPLETED
versus behind REVOKED. The first wording mixed the contract with the
signer's UI; this states only the contract.

Merge docs/what-remains-behind-each-terminal: the axis, published

A consumer was deriving from the code the one thing we owed them: what
the recipient still has behind COMPLETED versus behind REVOKED.

Merge origin/develop into docs/outbound-webhooks

Three conflicts, all both sides appending to a hand-kept index
(BACKLOG, the ADR README and the ddd README). Each resolves to the union.
The id spaces were checked before the merge.

docs(adr-0064): after ADR-0065 the delivery event says a destination failed, not which

A bounced invitation email and an accepted OTP SMS now coexist on one
recipient, so the webhook can no longer say that delivery failed for the
recipient as a whole.

Merge origin/develop and close the credential leak the merge exposed

This merge carries a behavioural change. The claimable axis in
SigningReadersRefuseUnsentEnvelopeTest went red: the resend
notification from TASK-041 is a fifth caller of
SigningTokenIssuer::issueFor() and had no answer on that axis, so it
could mail a credential for an unclaimed slot. It now refuses one.

test(task-036): cover the sender's ordinary case, a live envelope with an unreached step

Every claim test on a sent envelope put the slot on step 1, which send()
activates at once, so the common combination was never visited.

fix(observability): business refusals no longer reach Sentry as error events

Sentry's listener runs on kernel.exception at priority 128 and
ApiExceptionListener at 10, so Sentry saw the original throwable before
it was mapped to a status. Refusals that map to 4xx are now filtered
before sending.
Merge feat/claimable-recipient-slot into integration/claimable-delegated

Merge feat/delegated-signature onto develop and the claimable slot

An integration branch so the claimable slot and the delegated signature
can be exercised together against one running stack, based on
origin/develop.

feat(observability): tag Sentry releases with the build and report DDD signals

Events arrived with no release, so there was no first-seen, no
regression detection and no suspect commits; the image now carries which
code it is. Sentry also reads what the domain already says about itself
instead of leaving it unused (ADR-0009 part 2).

fix(delegated): an admission the recipient did not perform is not an opening

OnSigningSessionStarted sealed first_opened_at unconditionally, so a
delegated act recorded that someone had opened a link nobody was sent.
Also sweeps the prose the integration merge left stale.
Merge origin/develop into integration/claimable-delegated

Merge docs/outbound-webhooks: the webhook context designed

ADR-0064 and the webhook domain model describe tenant-scoped
subscriptions over a curated event catalog, delivered to an external
name. Nothing is built yet.

docs(adr-0064): the event census said 33 and the tree holds 36

Section 2.4 claims to classify every event the platform emits, which is
what makes the catalog curated; three events had been added since.

docs(storage): document the custody, custodian and retention decisions (1 of 12)

Records ADR-0061 (retention, deletion and purge under one COMPLIANCE
lock rolled by a custodian), ADR-0062 (stage, then promote) and
ADR-0063 (a stored object's identity is its custody).
build(storage): add the schema, roles and config for custody and the custodian (2 of 12)
feat(storage): add the Envelope and Storage contracts that custody builds on (3 of 12)
feat(storage): add the Storage domain: custody, placements and holds (4 of 12)
feat(storage): add the Storage application services and sweeps (5 of 12)
feat(storage): adapt Envelope, billing, bus and the custodian to custody (6 of 12)
feat(storage): add the DBAL custody repository and the S3 byte store (7 of 12)
test(storage): cover Envelope's use of custody in application tests (8 of 12)
test(storage): cover custody in foundation and cross-context tests (9 of 12)
test(storage): cover custody in Session and SignatureExecution tests (10 of 12)
test(storage): cover the custody repository, sweeps and S3 store (11 of 12)

test(storage): add the storage fakes, unit tests and event payloads (12 of 12)

Completes the storage module: a stored object is a custody, one
custodian keeps the lock, and staging is reclaimed by sweeps.

Merge feat/storage-custody-and-custodian: a stored object is a custody

ADR-0061/0062/0063 realized: the Storage module, the scheduled custodian
with its run records, and the sweeps that stage, promote, extend, mark
and destroy.

docs(style): drop the marks that repeated the bold beside them

Prose only: 91 comment and ADR lines, no behaviour touched.

docs(hygiene): point working-note labels at the sections that hold their claims

Prose only: 17 lines across 11 files, no behaviour touched.

fix(storage): correct records that called built machinery unbuilt, and four real defects

The pre-merge review's confirmed findings: most were prose, four were
not. Each was verified before it was changed.

fix(architecture): make the check read migrations and keep detectors honest

The architecture pass's confirmed findings: seventeen items, each
applied in the safe form rather than the first proposal.

fix(storage): one custody save is one transaction, with the finder its lock needs

DbalCustodyRepository::save() issues a statement for the root and one
for every placement and hold, so a caller-opened transaction has to
wrap them, and the locking finder reads under that same lock.

refactor(migrations): condense the branch's thirteen migrations into five, one per concern

The thirteen were written over eight days, each answering the question
in front of it. Read together they are five concerns. Safe to rewrite
because none had been pushed.

fix(storage): the filtered custody view runs as its invoker, so tenant isolation applies

storage.custody_live was a plain view, so it ran as its owner (the
migration superuser) and the isolation policy was never evaluated. The
lifecycle scenario also now seeds its frozen clock from the wall clock.

fix(step-order): refuse a recipient whose step is not active (TASK-042)

A recipient whose step the workflow had not reached could open a
session, authenticate, read and commit. One predicate, matched by step
id, now rides the recipient view onto the auth context and the open
(ADR-0066).

fix(step-order): the open, the auth routes and the seal refuse a dormant step

Links minted before the mint refused a dormant step still exist, and on
OTP_SMS every code sent to such a recipient is paid for. Sealing also
now asks for the frontier rather than a later step.

fix(step-order): the read model, document bytes and both commits refuse a dormant step

These were the last routes that served a dormant recipient everything,
including the commit that the preprod incident turned on. A census now
has a step axis over both of its universes.

test(step-order): reproduce the preprod incident over HTTP, and stop naming the recipient

DormantStepRefusedHttpTest seeds the three-step envelope of the
incident and shows the refusal. The refusal no longer names a recipient
in the problem detail, and the prose states the property, not a count.

docs(adr-0066): record that the realization landed and fix drifted counts

The Status stays Proposed; promotion is the maintainer's call. The
ddd models and the handoff index record the landing, and counts of
sites and routes are re-derived from the tree.

fix(session): the delegated commit refuses the assertion before the step

BL-263 gave the maintainer a choice between two readings of ADR-0066
2.6; this changes the code rather than the sentence. The records follow
the guard down and ADR-0066 is Accepted.
docs(tests): say what the order pin's fixture cannot assert

feat(session): a refused commit names its condition (TASK-043, ADR-0067)

Three refusals of POST /api/v1/signing/commit were byte-identical on the
wire because SigningSessionStateException implemented no ProblemCoded.
Each condition now has its own code; ADR-0067 records the decision.

test(session): each commit refusal is caught at its guard and named to the client

Application tests prove the refusal lands before anything is written;
acceptance tests prove four refusals arrive under four codes. A spent
signing code is now a 401, so the 409 stops claiming it.

docs(adr-0067,backlog): record the realization and close BL-249 and BL-259

Status stays Proposed. TASK-043 discharges both rows, and the records
are brought to the tip, which moved after the run they cited.

docs(task-043): correct the DSS failure cause and record the signer's side

StorageLifecycleScenarioTest was red because of the clock, not an
expired certificate: the development certificate runs to 2027-09-01.
The signer has applied both handoffs on its develop, unpushed.

Merge fix/step-order-at-every-door: no recipient acts before their step

TASK-042 / ADR-0066, Accepted. In preprod a three-step envelope let a
recipient of an unactivated step open, read and commit.

Merge fix/conflict-taxonomy: a refused commit names its condition

TASK-043 / ADR-0067, Accepted. The commit answered one bare CONFLICT for
five conditions and the signer sent them all to its done page.

docs(records): step-order and conflict-taxonomy are merged, not deployed

Eleven records still said not merged or not pushed. Merged is not
deployed, and the two changes go out in one deploy.
